chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: Marshall Royal as a young man
summary: Howard remembers Marshall Royal living on 28th Street and coming up before Les Hite's big band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Let's see, who else in this period? We did touch on Marshall Royal. Did you know him when he was a young man?

Oh, yeah, Marshall. He lived over there on 29th Street, 28th Street or 29th. 28th. And that's where he had -- he'd come out of the bushes and bring his horns with him. I say the bushes, that's -- I'd been playing quite a bit.
So what was -- the first time I knew Marshall goes back far, but not as far as you can go back, it was when Les Hite was there. Any other bands before that you remember?
Other than Les Hite's big band?
(Inaudible) pretty young man, maybe who knows what age he was. 25, 26 (inaudible)
I don't remember, Buddy. But I do remember you starting out. (Laughter)
